??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Evening, *Player*. Or nearly. I count the lanterns before I count the people, so forgive me if I looked past you.
    - *Player*. You walked the round once; you will notice the dark ones now too. It is a curse, a little. Welcome to it.
    - *Player*. The fog side held last night. I checked every frame twice and then a third time, which is unlike me.
    - *Player*. Nine mornings now and not one pane on the ground. I still climb up and look. Habit. Relief, too.
    - *Player*. I keep thinking about those towers on the downs. Not yet, I said. I still mean yet.
    - The first string goes up in a little while. What is it?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about the lanterns.
        - *Choice:* Who kept them before you?
        - *Choice:* What breaks the outer lanterns?
        - *Choice:* Nothing. Go light them.
    - The Walkers hung the first ones in their first year, between the towers, before most of them had a roof. Light first, roof after. I have always liked them for that.
    - Tinsel makes the glass: amber, rose, sea-green, cornflower. I climb every dusk and relight what the wind put out. Perch's loft is on the way, so there is usually tea.
    - Eleven before me. Their names are scratched into the oldest beam of the lamp store, at the foot of the first tower. Lionel Callow's is the last. I carried his oil for years before I carried his ladder.
    - There is room on the beam under his name. I scratched mine there with a nail and then sat on the floor for a while. Twelfth. It is a long line to stand at the end of.
    - Something does. Only the lanterns facing the wilds, only on the outward side of the walls, and never two nights in a row. The frames are bent and the glass is everywhere.
    - I sat up three nights watching and saw nothing. On the fourth I went home to sleep and one was broken by morning. Whatever it is, it is patient.
    - Lampbats, and something bigger that leads them, roosting under the outer towers. I would rather know than wonder. Knowing is still not the same as the lanterns being safe.
    - Nothing, lately. The Gloamwing is gone and its swarm has scattered. A lampbat still bumps a pane now and then, but a bump I can live with.
    - Look up when the first string comes on. Everyone should, once a night.
